claims.text: An integrated rapid-DSC and acoustic-emission combinatorial setup can accurately determine melting temperatures across compositionally graded HEAs.
The proposed setup can accurately determine the enthalpy of fusion.
The proposed setup can accurately determine the entropy of fusion.
Acoustic-emission monitoring can be used to determine volume changes at melting.
Liquid-phase thermodynamic properties can be inferred from systematic shifts in thermal and acoustic responses.
The method will typically achieve a melting-temperature uncertainty of approximately ±5 K.
The method will measure latent heat with 5–10% accuracy.
Compositionally graded transition-metal HEA thin films or chips can span a wide compositional space for high-throughput measurements.
Synchronizing combinatorial laser melting, rapid DSC, and acoustic-emission sensing enables real-time thermal and structural measurements during heating.
The experiments will use heating rates of 100–500 K/s.
Local compositional gradients act as intrinsic mediators in the combinatorial samples.
Acoustic-emission signals capture rapid volume expansion during melting.
Acoustic-emission signals capture structural reorganization during melting.
Distinct rapid-DSC endothermic peaks correspond to fusion events.
Mapping DSC and acoustic signals across a composition gradient permits extraction of fusion thermodynamic properties.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi is a well-characterized HEA benchmark studied using traditional containerless methods.
The approach is applicable to compositionally graded transition-metal HEAs.
Extremely fine microstructural variations or unconventional alloy systems may require additional calibration adaptations.
Calibration of acoustic-emission sensors is a primary source of measurement uncertainty.
Overlapping signals from adjacent compositional regions are a primary source of measurement uncertainty.
